title: 'Step 35: V7 ↔ V6 cathode daisy'

# Step 35: 5" wire daisy through V7 pin 8 (S), V7 pin 1 (S), V6 pin 1 (S), V6 pin 8

> *Strip both ends of a 5" wire ½". Feed one end through pin #8 (S) and connect it to pin #1 of V7 (S). Feed the other end through pin #1 (S) of V6 and connect to pin #8 of V6.* — manual page 8

## What you're doing physically

Mirror of [step 32](step-32-v2-v3-cathode-daisy.md), but for V7 and V6.

A 5" wire stripped ½" at each end. Threaded through V7 pin 8 on its way to V7 pin 1, and through V6 pin 1 on its way to V6 pin 8.

Both V7 pin 8 and V6 pin 1 are soldered (S) when the wire passes through them. V7 pin 1 is also soldered now (it has the 15.6 Ω from step 34 + this wire).

V6 pin 8 stays unsoldered for [step 36](step-36-v6-to-right-biaset.md).

## What this completes

V6 and V7 cathodes are now tied together and routed through the channel A 15.6 Ω sense resistor (from step 34) to ground. Identical topology to channel B (V2/V3 + 15.6 Ω, from steps 31-32).
